title: Compilation pipeline: source, IL, JIT, AOT
hook: A C# file is not executed as text. Roslyn emits IL into an assembly; the CLR JIT-compiles methods, or Native AOT compiles ahead of time. That is the opposite of `node app.mjs`.

sections.heading: Source → IL → machine code
sections.prose: You write `.cs` files. The C# compiler (Roslyn) produces Intermediate Language (IL) plus metadata, packaged as an assembly (`.dll`, sometimes an `.exe` shim). At run time the CLR’s JIT turns IL into native code per method, applying tiered compilation. Native AOT (`PublishAot`) compiles to a native binary before you deploy — useful for cold-start sensitive Lambdas, with a closed-world trim. JavaScript modules (`import`/`export`) are a load-time linking story inside one engine; a .NET assembly is a versioned, metadata-rich unit the loader binds. When two workers share a domain model, they share an assembly reference, not an npm package of `.ts` sources.

snippets.label: Same source, two publish modes
snippets.explanation: Interviewers want the split: compile to IL always (except AOT, which still starts from C# and produces native). JS has no IL assembly with CTS metadata.

sections.heading: Assembly versus JS module
sections.prose: An ES module is a file graph resolved by the host (Node, browser). A .NET assembly can contain many types, resources, and a strong name. Binding failures look like `FileNotFoundException` or version mismatches, not `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. For Redis or RabbitMQ client libraries you consume NuGet packages — assemblies — not `require()` of source. Async I/O on those clients still uses `Task`; that state machine is later (module 13). Here: the unit of deployment is the assembly (or an AOT binary), not a folder of modules.

interviewTakeaways: C# compile output is IL + metadata in an assembly; JIT or Native AOT produces CPU code.
Do not equate `import "./worker.js"` with referencing a .NET assembly.
AOT trades flexibility (reflection, runtime codegen) for startup and size — know when a consumer needs JIT instead.
commonPitfalls: Saying C# is “interpreted.” It is compiled; the JIT is a second compile, not a line-by-line interpreter.
Confusing the C# language version with the TFM. LangVersion is syntax; net10.0 is the runtime surface.
Assuming Native AOT is always on. SDK projects default to JIT unless you enable PublishAot (file-based apps enable it for publish).

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS modules are source/bytecode files the engine links. .NET assemblies are IL+metadata units versioned and loaded by the CLR.
